    <h1 class="devsite-page-title" tabindex="-1">
      Generate images using Imagen<devsite-actions hidden data-nosnippet>
    <devsite-llm-tools></devsite-llm-tools></devsite-actions>
  
      
    </h1>
  <div class="devsite-page-title-meta"><devsite-view-release-notes></devsite-view-release-notes></div>
  

  <devsite-toc class="devsite-nav"
    depth="2"
    devsite-toc-embedded
    >
  </devsite-toc>
  
    
  <div class="devsite-article-body clearfix
  ">

  
    
    
<p>
</p>

<p></p>


















<aside class="deprecated">
  This model is <a href="/gemini-api/docs/deprecations">deprecated</a> and will be shut down on August 17, 2026; migrate to Nano Banana for image generation.
</aside>

<p>Imagen is Google&#39;s high-fidelity image generation model, capable of generating
realistic and high quality images from text prompts. All generated images
include a SynthID watermark. To learn more about the available Imagen model
variants, see the <a href="#model-versions">Model versions</a> section.</p>
<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> You can also generate images with Gemini&#39;s built-in multimodal
capabilities. See the <a href="/gemini-api/docs/image-generation">Image generation
guide</a> for details.</span></aside>
<h2 id="migration-to-nano-banana" data-text="Migration to Nano Banana" tabindex="-1">Migration to Nano Banana</h2>

<p>Imagen models are deprecated and will shut down on August 17, 2026. We recommend
migrating to Nano Banana for your image generation needs.</p>

<p>Migration involves the following changes:</p>

<ul>
<li><strong>Model name</strong>: Use <code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-2.5-flash-image</code> instead of Imagen model names.</li>
<li><strong>Method</strong>: Use <code translate="no" dir="ltr">client.models.generate_content</code> instead of <code translate="no" dir="ltr">client.models.generate_images</code>.</li>
<li><strong>Response handling</strong>: Nano Banana returns content parts, which may include image data, instead of a specific image response object.</li>
</ul>

<p>See the <a href="/gemini-api/docs/image-generation">Image generation guide</a> for more
details and examples.</p>

<h2 id="imagen" data-text="Generate images using the Imagen models" tabindex="-1">Generate images using the Imagen models</h2>

<p>This example demonstrates generating images with an <a href="https://deepmind.google/technologies/imagen/">Imagen model</a>:</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="python" data-text="Python" tabindex="-1">Python</h3><div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="Python"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-kn">from</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nn">google</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-kn">import</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">genai</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-kn">from</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nn">google.genai</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-kn">import</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">types</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-kn">from</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nn">PIL</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-kn">import</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">Image</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-kn">from</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nn">io</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-kn">import</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">BytesIO</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-n">client</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">genai</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">Client</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">()</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-n">response</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">client</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">models</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">generate_images</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">(</span>
    <span class="devsite-syntax-n">model</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s1">'imagen-4.0-generate-001'</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>
    <span class="devsite-syntax-n">prompt</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s1">'Robot holding a red skateboard'</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>
    <span class="devsite-syntax-n">config</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">types</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">GenerateImagesConfig</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">(</span>
        <span class="devsite-syntax-n">number_of_images</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-mi">4</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>
    <span class="devsite-syntax-p">)</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-p">)</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-k">for</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">generated_image</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-ow">in</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">response</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">generated_images</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span>
  <span class="devsite-syntax-n">generated_image</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">image</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">show</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">()</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code></section>
<section><h3 id="javascript" data-text="JavaScript" tabindex="-1">JavaScript</h3><div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="JavaScript"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-k">import</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">GoogleGenAI</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">}</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-kr">from</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"@google/genai"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">;</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-k">import</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">*</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-kr">as</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">fs</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-kr">from</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"node:fs"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">;</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-k">async</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-kd">function</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">main</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">()</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-w">  </span><span class="devsite-syntax-kd">const</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">ai</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-ow">new</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">GoogleGenAI</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">({});</span>

<h3 id="imagen-configuration" data-text="Imagen configuration" tabindex="-1">Imagen configuration</h3>

<p>Imagen supports English only prompts at this time and the following parameters:</p>
<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> Naming conventions of parameters vary by programming language.</span></aside>
<ul>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">numberOfImages</code>: The number of images to generate, from 1 to 4 (inclusive).
The default is 4.</li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">imageSize</code>: The size of the generated image. This is only supported for
the Standard and Ultra models. The supported values are <code translate="no" dir="ltr">1K</code> and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">2K</code>.
Default is <code translate="no" dir="ltr">1K</code>.</li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">aspectRatio</code>: Changes the aspect ratio of the generated image. Supported
values are <code translate="no" dir="ltr">&quot;1:1&quot;</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">&quot;3:4&quot;</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">&quot;4:3&quot;</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">&quot;9:16&quot;</code>, and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">&quot;16:9&quot;</code>. The default is
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">&quot;1:1&quot;</code>.</li>
<li><p><code translate="no" dir="ltr">personGeneration</code>: Allow the model to generate images of people. The
following values are supported:</p>

<ul>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">&quot;dont_allow&quot;</code>: Block generation of images of people.</li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">&quot;allow_adult&quot;</code>: Generate images of adults, but not children. This is
the default.</li>
<li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">&quot;allow_all&quot;</code>: Generate images that include adults and children.</li>
</ul>
<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">&quot;allow_all&quot;</code> parameter value is not allowed in EU, UK, CH, MENA
    locations.</span></aside></li>
</ul>

<h2 id="imagen-prompt-guide" data-text="Imagen prompt guide" tabindex="-1">Imagen prompt guide</h2>

<p>This section of the Imagen guide shows you how modifying a text-to-image prompt
can produce different results, along with examples of images you can create.</p>

<h3 id="prompt-basics" data-text="Prompt writing basics" tabindex="-1">Prompt writing basics</h3>
<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> Maximum prompt length is 480 tokens.</span></aside>
<p>A good prompt is descriptive and clear, and makes use of meaningful keywords and
modifiers. Start by thinking of your <strong>subject</strong>, <strong>context</strong>, and <strong>style</strong>.</p>

<figure>
  <img src="/static/gemini-api/docs/images/imagen/style-subject-context.png" alt="Prompt with subject, context, and style emphasized" class="screenshot">
  <figcaption>Image text: A <i>sketch</i> (<b>style</b>) of a <i>modern apartment building</i>
(<b>subject</b>) surrounded by <i>skyscrapers</i> (<b>context and background</b>).</figcaption>
</figure>

<ol>
<li><p><strong>Subject</strong>: The first thing to think about with any prompt is the
<em>subject</em>: the object, person, animal, or scenery you want an image of.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Context and background:</strong> Just as important is the <em>background or context</em>
in which the subject will be placed. Try placing your subject in a variety
of backgrounds. For example, a studio with a white background, outdoors, or
indoor environments.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Style:</strong> Finally, add the style of image you want. <em>Styles</em> can be general
(painting, photograph, sketches) or very specific (pastel painting, charcoal
drawing, isometric 3D). You can also combine styles.</p></li>
</ol>

<p>After you write a first version of your prompt, refine your prompt by adding
more details until you get to the image that you want. Iteration is important.
Start by establishing your core idea, and then refine and expand upon that core
idea until the generated image is close to your vision.</p>

<table>
  <tr>
    <td>
      <figure>
      <img src="/static/gemini-api/docs/images/imagen/0_prompt-writing-basics_park_short.png"
             alt="photorealistic sample image 1"
             class="screenshot">
      <figcaption>Prompt: A park in the spring next to a lake</figcaption>
      </figure>
    </td>
    <td>
      <figure>
        <img src="/static/gemini-api/docs/images/imagen/0_prompt-writing-basics_park_medium.png"
             alt="photorealistic sample image 2"
             class="screenshot">
      <figcaption>Prompt: A park in the spring next to a lake, <b>the sun sets across the lake, golden hour</b></figcaption>
      </figure>
    </td>
    <td>
      <figure>
        <img src="/static/gemini-api/docs/images/imagen/0_prompt-writing-basics_park_long.png"
             alt="photorealistic sample image 3"
             class="screenshot">
      <figcaption>Prompt: A park in the spring next to a lake, <i><b>the sun sets across the lake, golden hour, red wildflowers</b></i></figcaption>
      </figure>
    </td>
  </tr>
</table>

<p>Imagen models can transform your ideas into detailed images, whether
your prompts are short or long and detailed. Refine your vision
through iterative prompting, adding details until you achieve the perfect
result.</p>

<table class="columns">
  <tr>
    <td>
      <div style="text-align: center;">
      <p>Short prompts let you generate an image quickly.</p>
      <figure>
        <img src="/static/gemini-api/docs/images/imagen/imagen3_short-prompt.png"
            alt="Imagen 4 short prompt example"
            class="screenshot">
        <figcaption>Prompt: close-up photo of a woman in her 20s, street photography,
        movie still, muted orange warm tones
        </figcaption>
      </figure>
      </div>
    </td>
    <td>
      <div style="text-align: center;">
      <p>Longer prompts let you add specific details and build your image.</p>
      <figure>
        <img src="/static/gemini-api/docs/images/imagen/imagen3_long-prompt.png"
            alt="Imagen 4 long prompt example"
            class="screenshot">
        <figcaption>Prompt: captivating photo of a woman in her 20s utilizing a street
        photography style. The image should look like a movie still with muted orange
        warm tones.
        </figcaption>
      </figure>
      </div>
    </td>
  </tr>
</table>

<p>Additional advice for Imagen prompt writing:</p>

<ul>
<li><strong>Use descriptive language</strong>: Employ detailed adjectives and adverbs to
paint a clear picture for Imagen.</li>
<li><strong>Provide context</strong>: If necessary, include background information to aid the
AI&#39;s understanding.</li>
<li><strong>Reference specific artists or styles</strong>: If you have a particular aesthetic
in mind, referencing specific artists or art movements can be helpful.</li>
<li><strong>Use prompt engineering tools</strong>: Consider exploring prompt engineering
tools or resources to help you refine your prompts and achieve optimal
results.</li>
<li><strong>Enhancing the facial details in your personal and group images</strong>: Specify facial details as a focus of the photo (for example, use the
    word &quot;portrait&quot; in the prompt).</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="generate-text" data-text="Generate text in images" tabindex="-1">Generate text in images</h3>

<p>Imagen models can add text into images, opening up more creative image generation
possibilities. Use the following guidance to get the most out of this feature:</p>

<ul>
<li><strong>Iterate with confidence</strong>: You might have to regenerate images until you
achieve the look you want. Imagen&#39;s text integration is still
evolving, and sometimes multiple attempts yield the best results.</li>
<li><strong>Keep it short</strong>: Limit text to 25 characters or less for optimal
generation.</li>
<li><p><strong>Multiple phrases</strong>: Experiment with two or three distinct phrases to
provide additional information. Avoid exceeding three phrases for cleaner
compositions.</p>

<figure>
<img src="/static/gemini-api/docs/images/imagen/imagen3_generate-text.png"
       alt="Imagen 4 generate text example"
       class="screenshot">
<figcaption>Prompt: A poster with the text "Summerland" in bold font as a
title, underneath this text is the slogan "Summer never felt so good"
</figcaption>
</figure></li>
<li><p><strong>Guide Placement</strong>: While Imagen can attempt to position text
as directed, expect occasional variations. This feature is continually
improving.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Inspire font style</strong>: Specify a general font style to subtly influence
Imagen&#39;s choices. Don&#39;t rely on precise font replication, but expect
creative interpretations.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Font size</strong>: Specify a font size or a general indication of size (for
example, <em>small</em>, <em>medium</em>, <em>large</em>) to influence the font size generation.</p></li>
</ul>

<h3 id="prompt-parameterization" data-text="Prompt parameterization" tabindex="-1">Prompt parameterization</h3>

<p>To better control output results, you might find it helpful to parameterize the
inputs into Imagen. For example, suppose you
want your customers to be able to generate logos for their business, and you
want to make sure logos are always generated on a solid color background. You
also want to limit the options that the client can select from a menu.</p>

<p>In this example, you can create a parameterized prompt similar to the
following:</p>

<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-disable-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded>A <var translate="no">{logo_style}</var> logo for a <var translate="no">{company_area}</var> company on a solid color background. Include the text <var translate="no">{company_name}</var>.</pre></devsite-code>

<p>In your custom user interface, the customer can input the parameters using
a menu, and their chosen value populates the prompt Imagen receives.</p>

<p>For example:</p>

<ol>
<li><p>Prompt: <code translate="no" dir="ltr">A <var translate="no">minimalist</var> logo for a <var translate="no">health care</var> company on a solid color background. Include the text <var translate="no">Journey</var>.</code></p>

<p><img src="/static/gemini-api/docs/images/imagen/imagen3_prompt-param_healthcare.png"
alt="Imagen 4 prompt parameterization example 1"
class="screenshot"></p></li>
<li><p>Prompt: <code translate="no" dir="ltr">A <var translate="no">modern</var> logo for a <var translate="no">software</var> company on a solid color background. Include the text <var translate="no">Silo</var>.</code></p>

<p><img src="/static/gemini-api/docs/images/imagen/imagen3_prompt-param_software.png"
alt="Imagen 4 prompt parameterization example 2"
class="screenshot"></p></li>
<li><p>Prompt: <code translate="no" dir="ltr">A <var translate="no">traditional</var> logo for a <var translate="no">baking</var> company on a solid color background. Include the text <var translate="no">Seed</var>.</code></p>

<p><img src="/static/gemini-api/docs/images/imagen/imagen3_prompt-param_baking.png"
alt="Imagen 4 prompt parameterization example 3"
class="screenshot"></p></li>
</ol>

<h3 id="advanced-prompts" data-text="Advanced prompt writing techniques" tabindex="-1">Advanced prompt writing techniques</h3>

<p>Use the following examples to create more specific prompts based on attributes
like photography descriptors, shapes and materials, historical art
movements, and image quality modifiers.</p>

<h4 id="img-quality-modifiers" data-text="Image quality modifiers" tabindex="-1">Image quality modifiers</h4>

<p>Certain keywords can let the model know that you&#39;re looking for a high-quality

<ul>
<li><strong>General Modifiers</strong> - <em>high-quality, beautiful, stylized</em></li>
<li><strong>Photos</strong> - <em>4K, HDR, Studio Photo</em></li>
<li><strong>Art, Illustration</strong> - <em>by a professional, detailed</em></li>
</ul>

<h4 id="aspect-ratios" data-text="Aspect ratios" tabindex="-1">Aspect ratios</h4>

<p>Imagen image generation lets you set five distinct image aspect
ratios.</p>

<ol>
<li><strong>Square</strong> (1:1, default) - A standard square photo. Common uses for this
aspect ratio include social media posts.</li>
<li><p><strong>Fullscreen</strong> (4:3) - This aspect ratio is commonly used in media or film.
It is also the dimensions of most old (non-widescreen) TVs and medium format
cameras. It captures more of the scene horizontally (compared to 1:1),
making it a preferred aspect ratio for photography.</p>

<table class="columns">
<tr>
<td>
<figure>
<img src="/static/gemini-api/docs/images/imagen/aspect-ratios_4-3_piano.png"
        alt="aspect ratio example"
        class="screenshot">
<figcaption>Prompt: close up of a musician's fingers
playing the piano, black and white film, vintage (4:3 aspect ratio)
</figcaption>
</figure>
</td>
<td>
<figure>
<img src="/static/gemini-api/docs/images/imagen/aspect-ratios_4-3_fries.png"
        alt="aspect ratio example"
        class="screenshot">
<figcaption>Prompt: A professional studio photo of
french fries for a high end restaurant, in the style of a food magazine
     (4:3 aspect ratio)
</figcaption>
</figure>
</td>
</tr>
</table></li>
<li><p><strong>Portrait full screen</strong> (3:4) - This is the fullscreen aspect ratio rotated
90 degrees. This lets to capture more of the scene vertically compared to
the 1:1 aspect ratio.</p>

<table class="columns">
<tr>
<td>
<figure>
<img src="/static/gemini-api/docs/images/imagen/aspect-ratios_3-4_hiking.png"
        alt="aspect ratio example"
        class="screenshot">
<figcaption>Prompt: a woman hiking, close of her
boots reflected in a puddle, large mountains in the background, in the
style of an advertisement, dramatic angles (3:4 aspect ratio)
</figcaption>
</figure>
</td>
<td>
<figure>
<img src="/static/gemini-api/docs/images/imagen/aspect-ratios_3-4_valley.png"
        alt="aspect ratio example"
        class="screenshot">
<figcaption>Prompt: aerial shot of a river flowing
up a mystical valley (3:4 aspect ratio)
</figcaption>
</figure>
</td>
</tr>
</table></li>
<li><p><strong>Widescreen</strong> (16:9) - This ratio has replaced 4:3 and is now the most
common aspect ratio for TVs, monitors, and mobile phone screens (landscape).
Use this aspect ratio when you want to capture more of the background (for
example, scenic landscapes).</p>

<figure>
<img src="/static/gemini-api/docs/images/imagen/aspect-ratios_16-9_man.png"
       alt="aspect ratio example"
       class="screenshot">
<figcaption>Prompt: a man wearing all white
clothing sitting on the beach, close up, golden hour lighting (16:9
aspect ratio)
</figcaption>
</figure></li>
<li><p><strong>Portrait</strong> (9:16) - This ratio is widescreen but rotated. This a
relatively new aspect ratio that has been popularized by short form video
apps (for example, YouTube shorts). Use this for tall objects with strong
vertical orientations such as buildings, trees, waterfalls, or other similar
objects.</p>

<figure>
<img src="/static/gemini-api/docs/images/imagen/aspect-ratios_9-16_skyscraper.png"
       alt="aspect ratio example"
       class="screenshot">
<figcaption>Prompt: a digital render of a massive skyscraper, modern,
grand, epic with a beautiful sunset in the background (9:16 aspect ratio)
</figcaption>
</figure></li>
</ol>

<h4 id="photorealistic" data-text="Photorealistic images" tabindex="-1">Photorealistic images</h4>

<p>Different versions of the image generation
model might offer a mix of artistic and photorealistic output. Use the following
wording in prompts to generate more photorealistic output, based on the subject
you want to generate.</p>
<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> Take these keywords as general guidance when you try to create
photorealistic images. They aren&#39;t required to achieve your goal.</span></aside>
<table>
 <thead>
   
    
   <tr>
     <th>Use case</th>
